anomalies.observed: R6 is a 10K pull-up resistor connected between the VCC net and the RST net. RST connects to the reset pins of U2 (ATtiny45) and U3 (ATtiny13). VCC is the input voltage to the LM1117-5.0 regulator, so it is higher than 5V.
anomalies.expected: The reset pull-up should be connected to the +5V regulated supply, which is the VCC of the ATtiny microcontrollers, not to the unregulated VCC input. Pulling reset to VCC can exceed the maximum voltage rating of the MCU pins.

evidence.quote: R6 10K between VCC and RST; U2 ATtiny45-20P pin 1 RESET/PB5 connects to RST; U3 ATtiny13V-10S pin 1 RESET/PB5 connects to RST; U1 LM1117-5.0 input VCC output +5V

anomalies.impact: The reset pins of U2 and U3 will be pulled to VCC (likely >5V), which may damage the microcontrollers or cause unreliable reset operation. The internal protection diodes may clamp and draw excessive current.

anomalies.observed: J1 (I2C connector) pin 2 is labeled SCL. U2 pin 7 and U3 pin 7 are labeled SCK. There is no wire or label connecting SCL to SCK; they are separate nets.
anomalies.expected: The I2C clock line from J1 should connect to the SCL pin (PB2) of the ATtiny microcontrollers (U2 pin 7, U3 pin 7). The net should be named consistently (e.g., SCL or SCK) and connected.

evidence.quote: J1 I2C pin 2 labeled SCL; U2 pin 7 labeled SCK; U3 pin 7 labeled SCK; no connection between SCL and SCK

anomalies.impact: The microcontrollers will not receive the I2C clock signal, so I2C communication with the fan controller will fail.

anomalies.observed: Q2 is an NPN transistor (BC817). Its base is connected via R4 to the TACH net, which connects to U3 pin 2 (PB4) of the ATtiny13. Its collector is connected to J2 pin 3 (TACH_IN) and pulled up via R2 to VCC. Its emitter is grounded. Thus, the MCU drives the base, and the fan tach line is on the collector.
anomalies.expected: For the MCU to read the fan tachometer signal, the fan tach line should drive the base (or be directly connected to the MCU input with a pull-up), and the MCU should read the collector (or the direct line). The MCU should not drive the fan tach line.

evidence.quote: Q2 BC817: base connected to R4 -> TACH (U3.2); collector connected to J2.3 (TACH_IN) and R2 pull-up to VCC; emitter to GND

anomalies.impact: The tachometer input circuit is non-functional. The MCU will drive the fan's tach output line, potentially causing contention with the fan's open-collector output. The MCU will not be able to read the fan speed.

parsed.summary: The schematic contains multiple serious errors: the reset pull-up R6 connects to the unregulated VCC instead of +5V, the I2C clock net from J1 (SCL) is not connected to the MCU pins (SCK), and the fan tachometer transistor Q2 has its base and collector swapped, preventing tach reading.
